name: Script Adherence Monitor
tagline: Every required disclosure, verified on every call
shortDescription: Continuous monitoring that checks 100% of calls against your regulatory scripts, mandatory disclosures, and prohibited-language rules — with evidence-linked findings, not spot checks.
longDescription:
Most compliance teams audit 1-3% of calls and hope the sample is representative. When a regulator asks whether the Mini-Miranda was read, whether the recording disclosure was given, or whether the cooling-off terms were explained, a sample is not an answer. Script Adherence Monitor reviews every call, every day, against the exact wording requirements your legal team defines.

You model each requirement as a rule: mandatory phrases, ordered sequences (identity verification before account details), conditional disclosures (only when a sale occurs), and prohibited language. Homayar's compliance agents transcribe each call, locate where each rule was satisfied or missed, and attach the timestamped transcript segment as evidence. Supervisors see a per-call adherence score; compliance officers see trend lines by team, campaign, and rule.

Because Homayar is a companion rather than a surveillance tool, findings route first to the agent and their supervisor as a correctable coaching item — not as an automatic mark on a record. Repeat misses escalate on a schedule you configure, so agents get the chance to self-correct before compliance ever intervenes. Teams using this pattern typically see adherence climb within the first two scoring cycles, without the morale cost of gotcha-style QA.

Rule libraries ship pre-built for collections (FDCPA), insurance sales, banking disclosures, and healthcare intake, and every library is fully editable. Audit exports are formatted for regulator and internal-audit consumption out of the box.
whoItsFor: Compliance officers, risk managers, and QA leaders at regulated contact centers — banking, collections, insurance, and healthcare operations that must prove script adherence to auditors.

name: PCI & PII Redaction Engine
tagline: Sensitive data removed before anyone hears it
shortDescription: Automatic detection and redaction of card numbers, national IDs, health identifiers, and personal data from call audio and transcripts — applied before storage, search, or review.
longDescription:
Every recorded call is a liability surface. Card numbers read aloud during payment, national ID numbers given for verification, diagnosis details shared during a claims call — once they land in a recording archive, they are in scope for PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR, and every person with playback access becomes part of your risk model.

The Redaction Engine sits at the front of the Homayar pipeline. As audio is ingested, detection models identify PANs, CVVs, IBANs, national identifiers, dates of birth, addresses, and health information in both the transcript and the underlying audio. Matched segments are masked in text and replaced with tone or silence in audio before the call ever reaches storage, search indexes, QA review queues, or AI analysis. The original sensitive spans are never persisted.

Detection combines pattern validation (Luhn checks on card numbers, country-specific ID formats) with contextual models that catch data read out of order, spelled letter by letter, or embedded in conversational phrasing — the cases regex-only tools miss. Each redaction event is logged with type, timestamp, and confidence, giving your assessor a complete, queryable redaction record.

For QSA audits, the module produces a scope-reduction report documenting that cardholder data is not retained in the recording environment — frequently the single largest factor in shrinking PCI scope for a contact center.
whoItsFor: Information security leaders, data protection officers, and compliance teams at organizations that record calls involving payments, identity verification, or health information.

name: Executive Insights Report
tagline: Ninety days of calls, distilled for leadership
shortDescription: A one-time, analyst-grade report built from up to 90 days of your call data: the issues driving volume, the moments costing revenue, and the actions ranked by impact.
longDescription:
Leadership teams rarely lack call data — they lack a defensible reading of it. The Executive Insights Report is a one-time engagement: you connect or upload up to 90 days of recorded calls, and Homayar's agent team performs a full analysis pass — transcription, issue classification, sentiment and escalation mapping, quality scoring, and root-cause clustering across every conversation.

The output is a 30-40 page report written for an executive audience. It opens with the five findings that matter most, each backed by call volume, trend direction, and estimated cost or revenue impact. It maps your top contact drivers against resolution rates, identifies the process failures generating repeat calls, quantifies where customers churn-signal inside conversations, and benchmarks quality variance across teams and sites.

Every claim in the report links back to evidence: anonymized call excerpts, frequency counts, and confidence levels. The final section is a prioritized action register — typically 8-12 recommendations ranked by estimated impact and implementation effort, written so an ops leader can assign owners the same week.

Most buyers use this report one of three ways: as the business case for a broader analytics rollout, as board-level evidence for a CX investment decision, or as an annual independent read on operational health. Delivery is within 10 business days of data access.

name: KPI Dashboard Builder
tagline: Your metrics, your layout, live from every call
shortDescription: A drag-and-drop builder for live dashboards over Homayar call analytics — compose quality, sentiment, compliance, and resolution metrics into views for each role on your team.
longDescription:
Every operations team measures differently. A collections floor watches promise-to-pay and adherence; a telecom support desk watches first-contact resolution and handle-time outliers; a sales team watches talk ratios and objection patterns. One fixed dashboard cannot serve all of them — so the KPI Dashboard Builder lets each team compose its own.

Start from a library of 40+ metric widgets computed continuously from analyzed calls: quality scores, sentiment trajectories, issue frequencies, script adherence, silence and hold ratios, escalation rates, coaching-flag counts, and more. Drag widgets onto a grid, filter each one by team, campaign, queue, date range, or call tag, and choose its visualization — trend line, distribution, leaderboard, heatmap, or single-stat tile.

Dashboards are role-aware. A supervisor's view drills from team rollups into individual calls with transcript evidence one click away. An agent's personal view shows their own trends against team medians — framed as a progress companion, never a public ranking wall. Executives get rollup views with site and region comparisons. Each dashboard carries its own access scope, so agents see what helps them and nothing that polices them.

Every dashboard supports scheduled email snapshots, shareable read-only links for stakeholders outside the platform, and CSV export of any widget's underlying data.

longDescription:
The hardest report to produce is the one due every quarter. Numbers must reconcile with the last pack, narratives must explain variance rather than restate it, and the whole document must survive a CFO's scrutiny. The Board Pack Reporting Plan turns that recurring burden into a subscription service with a human in the loop.

On your chosen cadence — monthly or quarterly — Homayar compiles a board pack from your live call analytics: quality and adherence trends, contact-driver shifts, customer-sentiment movement, cost-per-resolution indicators, and progress against the targets your leadership set. Each pack is then reviewed by a Homayar analyst, who verifies metric continuity with prior periods, writes the variance commentary, and flags anomalies worth a leadership conversation before they become surprises.

Packs follow your template: your logo, your section order, your KPI definitions. Period-over-period deltas are computed automatically, and every figure is traceable to the underlying call data — so when a board member asks where a number came from, the answer is one link away.

The plan includes a quarterly definitions review with your team to keep KPIs aligned as the operation evolves, and priority support for ad-hoc data requests that arrive mid-cycle, because board questions rarely wait for the next pack.

name: AI Coaching Plans
tagline: A personal development plan for every agent
shortDescription: Per-agent coaching plans generated from each agent's own calls: specific skill gaps, example moments, practice exercises, and measurable targets — refreshed every scoring cycle.
longDescription:
Most coaching fails for a simple reason: it is generic. An agent hears "work on empathy" in a monthly one-on-one, with no example, no exercise, and no way to know if they improved. AI Coaching Plans replaces that with evidence-based development built from each agent's actual conversations.

After every scoring cycle, Homayar's coaching agents analyze each agent's calls and identify their two or three highest-leverage growth areas — not a laundry list, but the specific skills whose improvement would move their outcomes most. Each growth area comes with timestamped moments from the agent's own calls showing the pattern, a contrast example of the skill done well (drawn from anonymized top-quartile calls in your own operation), a concrete practice exercise, and a measurable target for the next cycle.

Supervisors receive a coaching brief before each one-on-one: what to discuss, which call moments to play, and what was agreed last time — turning a vague check-in into a 20-minute structured session. Agents see their own plan and their own trend lines, framed as a companion to their growth rather than a verdict on their performance. Nothing in the plan feeds disciplinary workflows.

Across cycles, the module tracks skill movement per agent and per team, so training leaders can see which coaching themes are landing and which need a different approach.
whoItsFor: Team leads, QA coaches, and training managers responsible for agent development — especially teams where supervisors coach 10-20 agents each and preparation time is scarce.

name: Onboarding Accelerator
tagline: New agents proficient in weeks, not months
shortDescription: An implementation service that builds a curated call library, scenario curriculum, and milestone scoring track from your own best conversations — so new hires learn from what good actually sounds like.
longDescription:
New-agent ramp is one of the most expensive line items in any contact center: 8-12 weeks to proficiency, elevated error rates throughout, and attrition concentrated in the first 90 days. Most onboarding fails because it teaches policy instead of conversation. New hires read scripts and shadow a random colleague — they rarely hear a structured progression of what excellent actually sounds like.

The Onboarding Accelerator is a fixed-scope implementation. Homayar analyzes your historical calls and identifies your genuinely best conversations across your top contact types — the de-escalation handled cleanly, the complex billing dispute resolved in one call, the objection turned into a save. These become a curated, annotated call library: each example tagged by scenario, skill, and difficulty, with key moments highlighted and explained.

Around the library, we build a milestone curriculum mapped to your contact mix: listen-and-annotate exercises in week one, scenario comparisons in week two, then live-call scoring against a new-hire rubric that tightens as the agent progresses. Homayar scores every new-hire call from day one, so trainers see exactly which skills each cohort member has landed and which need intervention — long before the traditional week-six review.

Delivery takes 4-6 weeks and includes trainer enablement, so your team owns and extends the curriculum after handoff. The library refreshes automatically as new exemplary calls are detected in production.
whoItsFor: Training managers, onboarding leads, and operations directors at contact centers hiring in cohorts — particularly those with seasonal ramps or persistent early-tenure attrition.

name: CRM & Helpdesk Connector Pack
tagline: Call intelligence inside the tools you already use
shortDescription: Bi-directional connectors for Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Freshdesk, and ServiceNow — call scores, summaries, and detected issues appear on the records your teams already work in.
longDescription:
Analysis that lives in a separate tab is analysis that gets ignored. Supervisors work in the helpdesk; account teams work in the CRM. If a call's quality score, summary, and detected issues are not visible on the ticket or the contact record, they might as well not exist for the person who needs them.

The Connector Pack syncs Homayar output into Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Freshdesk, and ServiceNow. Each analyzed call is matched to its ticket, case, or contact using your existing identifiers — case ID, phone number, or interaction reference — and writes back a structured payload: AI summary, quality score, sentiment trajectory, detected issues, compliance flags, and a deep link to the full transcript and audio moments in Homayar.

The sync runs both directions. CRM and helpdesk context — customer tier, product line, open-case status, account value — flows into Homayar and becomes available as analysis dimensions, so you can ask questions like "how does sentiment trend on calls from enterprise-tier customers with an open P1?" Field mapping is fully configurable, and you control exactly which Homayar outputs are written to which objects, including the option to exclude agent-level scores from CRM visibility entirely — companion, not surveillance, extends to where the data lands.

Setup for a standard object model takes under a day per platform. Custom objects and on-premise ServiceNow instances are supported through the configuration layer.
whoItsFor: CX operations managers, CRM administrators, and IT teams who want call intelligence embedded in existing agent and supervisor workflows instead of another login.

name: CCaaS Ingestion Connectors
tagline: Every platform's calls, flowing into one analyzer
shortDescription: Enterprise ingestion from Genesys Cloud, Five9, NICE CXone, Amazon Connect, Twilio Flex, Avaya, and SIPREC sources — with metadata mapping, backfill, and a guaranteed onboarding path.
longDescription:
Before any call can be analyzed, it has to arrive — reliably, with its metadata intact, from whatever mix of platforms your operation runs. For most enterprises that mix is genuinely messy: a primary CCaaS platform, a legacy PBX at two acquired sites, an outsourcer on a different stack, and an archive of historical recordings in object storage. The CCaaS Ingestion Connectors module is how all of it reaches Homayar.

Native connectors cover Genesys Cloud, Five9, NICE CXone, Amazon Connect, Twilio Flex, and Avaya, pulling recordings and interaction metadata — queue, agent, ANI/DNIS, wrap-up codes, transfer chains — through each platform's APIs as calls complete. For on-premise and SBC-based estates, a SIPREC recording interface captures calls at the network layer. Batch pipelines ingest historical archives from S3, Azure Blob, or SFTP, preserving original timestamps so trend analysis reaches back before day one.

Metadata from every source is normalized into a single schema, so a call from Five9 and a call from an Avaya site are filterable, comparable, and reportable side by side. Ingestion is monitored end to end: per-source volume baselines, gap detection when a feed goes quiet, and automatic backfill when a platform's API recovers from an outage.

Because every enterprise estate differs — platform versions, recording topologies, data-residency constraints, outsourcer access agreements — this module is scoped and priced per environment, with a dedicated integration engineer and a committed onboarding timeline in the statement of work.
